native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The factor of -0.9568 for BA degree completion is the log-odds contrast between Black and White respondents: Black respondents have a BA-completion factor of -0.9568 relative to White respondents (equivalently White vs Black is +0.9568), reflecting substantially lower odds of BA completion among Black (1.33%) than White (3.54%) respondents, with Hispanic (1.44%) in between. Diagnostic note: no specification fitted to the supplied CSV reproduces -0.9568 exactly (closest: Black vs White = -0.9830 Poisson GLM, -0.9908 Firth logit, -1.0057 unadjusted logit; Hispanic vs White never below -0.93 pooled), so the exact value likely comes from the original analysis's richer specification (e.g., the curriculum variable named in the dataset description but absent from the CSV); the adjustment-path evidence identifies the Black-vs-White contrast as the one on which -0.9568 is attainable.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows, 100% complete cases, no coded-out values); tabulated race frequencies (White 5337, Black 2113, Hispanic 1323), BA distribution (236 True / 8537 False) and BA rates by race (White 3.54%, Hispanic 1.44%, Black 1.33%). 2) Primary scan: logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race indicators with all 3 reference encodings, covariate-free and adjusted (SES, ASVAB composite, PERCENTILE IN CLASS, sex, family size); enumerated all pairwise log-odds contrasts; no match to -0.9568. 3) Fallbacks (2,700+ contrasts): linear probability model, probit, complementary log-log, Poisson GLM, Firth penalized logit, all covariate subsets, pairwise two-race subset logits, per-sex strata, race-x-sex and race-x-covariate interactions, multinomial logit of race, BA-by-race slope models, penalized and nonlinear/discretized variants — zero exact matches. 4) Closest matches: Black vs White -0.9830 (Poisson), -0.9908 (Firth), -1.0057 (logit race-only); Hispanic vs White -0.9284 (logit+sex), -0.9241 (race-only). 5) Structural identification via adjustment-path analysis: -0.9568 is attainable only on the Black-vs-White path (which runs from -1.0057 toward -0.86 as controls are added), never on the Hispanic-vs-White path; combined with the dataset description referencing a curriculum control absent from the CSV, the pair is Black and White, direction Black relative to White.

sub_hypo.relations: BA completion is less likely among Black than White respondents, with Hispanic respondents intermediate. The proposed Black-versus-White log-odds contrast is -0.9568, but no fitted specification reproduces it exactly.

sub_hypo.text: Adjustment-path evidence identifies Black relative to White, rather than Hispanic relative to White, as the contrast on which -0.9568 is attainable. The exact value likely derives from a richer original specification, potentially including curriculum, which is absent from the supplied CSV.
sub_hypo.context: Regression and adjustment-path analyses of the supplied NLS CSV, considering socioeconomic status, ASVAB composite, class percentile, sex, and family size as controls.
sub_hypo.relations: The Black-versus-White log-odds contrast moves from -1.0057 toward -0.86 as controls are added, placing -0.9568 on its adjustment path; the Hispanic-versus-White path does not attain -0.9568, with pooled contrasts never below -0.93. Closest reported Black-versus-White estimates are -0.9830 from Poisson GLM, -0.9908 from Firth logit, and -1.0057 from unadjusted logit. A richer original specification is a proposed explanation, not a reproduced result.
